newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila eyes more regulation on real estate loans.
newsitem.headline: Manila eyes more regulation on real estate loans.

text.p: Philippine Central Bank governor Gabriel Singson said on Thursday that the bank is considering additional regulations on bank loans to the real estate sector, especially those operating in Metro Manila.

"The Central Bank is ... considering additional regulations on Metro Manila property valuations of banks for loan purposes to further safeguard the banking system in the event of corrections in the real estate market," Singson told a group of financial executives.
A recent study made by the Central Bank said banks should limit their loan exposures to the real estate sector since its recent expansion could build up inflationary pressures.

Among the recommendations were the imposition of a single industry exposure limit equivalent to 50 percent of the bank's net worth and the setting up of probable losses equivalent to 25 percent of the loans.
The study showed that credits to real estate projects were at an average of 9.2 percnet of the total loan portfolio of banks.
